newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada gas marketer sues would-be acquisitor.
newsitem.headline: Canada gas marketer sues would-be acquisitor.

text.p: A Canadian independent natural gas marketer said on Tuesday it was launching a C$25-million lawsuit against a U.S.-controlled firm which had previously agreed to purchase it but walked away from the deal.

Calgary-based Brymore Energy Ltd, which marketed about 100 million cubic feet per day of gas and had annual revenues of about C$60 million, said its business was to be sold to UtiliCorp Energy Services Ltd, a subsidiary of Kansas City-based UtiliCorp United Inc, in a deal slated for closing on Monday.
UtiliCorp said on Tuesday it refused to close the deal after Brymore did not meet conditions of the sale.
Don Snyder, who was chairman of Brymore, said in an interview that UtiliCorp had failed to meet its obligations by backing out of the deal "at the 11th hour."
All of Brymore's purchase, sale, gas transportation contracts and regulatory permits had already been transferred to UtiliCorp effective November 1, he said.

The legal action is the latest in a series of recent controversies involving small Canadian gas marketers, some of which went bankrupt after facing cash crunches when the price of Canadian natural gas doubled in November.

Richard Hornowski, secretary of UtiliCorp Energy, said Brymore failed to meet "certain preconditions" for the deal to close, so no money changed hands. He declined to elaborate on the nature of the preconditions.

"We make our position clear, which is the transaction did not close and, given that the transaction did not close, we do not own any of the contracts or assets of Brymore, we have not paid for them and they were not able to meet the preconditions of closing," Hornowski said.
He would not comment on the state of Brymore's finances in the time leading up to the expected close date.

Snyder said that, while most small gas marketers were finding it almost impossible to trade in today's market because of the demand for -- and firms' little ability to get -- top-rated credit, Brymore had not been headed for financial failure and was profitable for the last two months.
Hornowski said UtiliCorp had not decided whether it would launch a countersuit.
"We'll take whatever actions are available. If they believe they have a claim, then clearly we'll have to proceed," he said.
"But we're not about to act precipitously -- there's been enough uncertainty in the gas markets in Calgary over the last little while."

The last two months have been financially brutal for Canada's small gas marketing companies. In November, private marketer Multi-Energies Inc went bankrupt, newly formed NESI Energy Marketing Canada Ltd filed for protection from creditors and Tarpon Gas Marketing Ltd was placed into receivership.

Also, Kentucky-based LG&E Natural Inc, a unit of LG&E Energy Corp, launched a C$210-million lawsuit against the former vice-president of its Canadian subsidiary, alleging he made unauthorized trades resulting in losses of US$17 million. The executive has argued he was authorized to make the trades. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
